source_refs.note: Book p. 49: 4.2.1 Addition of Matrices (conformable for addition, c_ij = a_ij + b_ij). The book gives no example here; the worked illustrations, Teaching notes, Key points and Common mistake are ours.

blocks.text: Two matrices are conformable for addition if they are of the same order.

The sum \(A + B\) of two \(m \times n\) matrices \(A = [a_{ij}]\) and \(B = [b_{ij}]\) is the \(m \times n\) matrix \(C = [c_{ij}]\) formed by adding the corresponding entries of \(A\) and \(B\) together. In symbols, we write \(C = A + B\), that is:

blocks.text_alt: c i j equals a i j plus b i j, entry by entry

blocks.text: where \(c_{ij} = a_{ij} + b_{ij}\) for \(i = 1, 2, 3, \ldots, m;\ j = 1, 2, 3, \ldots, n\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: "Conformable" means "fit to be combined". Every entry of \(A\) needs a partner in the same position in \(B\); that is only possible when both matrices have the same number of rows and the same number of columns. The sum has the same order as \(A\) and \(B\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Our example (not from the book):
\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix}5 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix} 1+5 & 2+(-1) \\ 3+0 & 4+2 \end{bmatrix}\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix}6 & 1 \\ 3 & 6\end{bmatrix}\]
Each entry of the answer is the sum of the two entries in the same position. Adding in the other order gives the same matrix, because each entry is an ordinary sum of numbers: \(A + B = B + A\) (see 4.3).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Not defined: \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 5 & 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\). The orders \(2 \times 2\) and \(2 \times 3\) differ, so the third column of the second matrix has nothing to be added to. We simply say the sum is not defined.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. \(A + B\) is defined only when \(A\) and \(B\) have the same order.
2. Add corresponding entries: \(c_{ij} = a_{ij} + b_{ij}\).
3. The sum has the same order as \(A\) and \(B\).

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text:
1. Adding matrices of different orders (for example by padding with zeros). The sum is simply not defined.
2. Adding entries that are not in the same position, such as row 1 of \(A\) with column 1 of \(B\).
3. Losing the signs of negative entries: \(2 + (-1) = 1\), not 3.
